title: Contractive scalar units in continuous integral coefficients
statement: Let ℓ be prime and E a normed field with a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra structure. For any scheme X, a commutative internal ring R isomorphic by a ring homomorphism e to the continuous integral coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and any R-linear endomorphism f of the regular R-module, the endomorphism 1−ℓf is invertible. There are no noetherianity or finite dimensionality assumptions.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, Section 6.8, continuous coefficient realization and integral units

proof.text: Generalize the proved continuous-ring comparison construction from CondensedFieldLfpLocalTriviality to any totally disconnected topological ring in Type 0. Define its adjoint using the existing profiniteTestProjection |X[S]|→S and reuse profiniteTestProjection_natural from the same module. It is a ring homomorphism. On an affine weakly contractible test object, the point-components comparison and unchanged sheafification sections make it an isomorphism; the affine weakly contractible covering family detects that it is an isomorphism on all test objects. Import and reuse its existing generic projection naturality, point-components target naturality, affine weakly contractible detection and pushforward-ring helpers; only the coefficient-ring generalization is proved here.

A morphism of regular modules is sectionwise linear: applying the sheaf tensor comparison to the module action equation proves f_U(ab)=a f_U(b). Hence on every test object it is multiplication by the continuous integral function f_U(1).

The normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra is ultrametric, and ||ℓ||<1. Thus for every integral a, ||1−ℓa||=1. For a continuous integral-valued function a, its pointwise reciprocal (1−ℓa)⁻¹ is continuous, integral, and inverse on both sides. This constructs a unit without requiring completeness of E.

The integral coefficient ring is totally disconnected by the ultrametric topology. Use the continuous-ring comparison and sectionwise linearity to show every component of 1−ℓf is multiplication by a unit, hence bijective. Reflect the component isomorphisms through sheaves and internal module forgetting. Finally transport the result across e using the proved Mod.regularIsoOfIsIso comparison for restriction of scalars.

proof_origin.note: Fully proved. Only the already proved continuous comparison helpers are generalized from the field-local-triviality module; its remaining finite-free-cover sorry is neither copied nor used. The comparison is constructed, not chosen from an existence sorry. Return repair: generic coefficient-independent helpers are imported directly from CondensedFieldLfpLocalTriviality rather than copied. No field local-freeness assertion is applied. Fresh second reading: also remove the renamed projection construction and its naturality proof, using existing profiniteTestProjection and profiniteTestProjection_natural directly.
